# PokéAPI domain fixtures

`domain-captures.json` contains responses captured from `https://pokeapi.co/api/v2/` on 2026-09-30. Evolution chains 1, 2, 47, 67, 280, 287, 352, and 362 retain every upstream field and alternative. The item, Pokémon, species, and ability entries retain the fields consumed by the dossier and item services; English text entries are selected and Pokémon move lists are limited to two entries to keep these domain tests focused. The Pokémon entries' `past_abilities`, `past_stats`, and `past_types` were captured on 2026-11-25, as were those of the Pokémon records in `resolution-captures.json`.

`syntheticDetail` deliberately populates every documented evolution-detail field, including conditional-expression data absent from the captured chains. Tests that attach another chain to the Bulbasaur fixture are normalization probes, not Pokémon game-data claims.

Shape references: [EvolutionDetail](https://pokeapi.co/docs/v2/#evolution-chains), [ItemPrice](https://pokeapi.co/docs/v2/#items).

`resolution-captures.json` contains successful PokéAPI responses captured on 2026-10-14: Deoxys and Wormadam records, species, dependencies, type memberships, and generation lists. Records retain the fields read by the service; Pokémon moves are limited to two entries, and species/ability text is English-only. Complete type and generation memberships preserve the Psychic/Generation III intersection of 20 species.

`generation-captures.json` contains PokéAPI responses captured on 2026-11-25 for generation-scoped type matchups: the generation catalog and all nine generations (ID, name, introduced types, version groups), all 21 types (introduction generation, current and past damage relations), and Clefairy, Magnemite, Rotom-Heat, Garchomp, and Alolan Raichu with their form records. `generation-fixtures.ts` exposes them as `handlerHttp` overrides, routing each generation by its numeric ID as well as its name.

`machine-captures.json` contains PokéAPI responses captured on 2026-11-25: the TM25 item and Earthquake move (English effect text only; Earthquake's learners limited to two), all 51 machine records their machine rows reference, and the Legends: Arceus version group. TM25 has 25 machine rows and Earthquake 26, the most any item or move carries. The five items in `domain-captures.json` carry upstream's empty `machines` list.

`effect-text-captures.json` contains PokéAPI responses captured on 2026-11-25 for records without English effect prose: the Blood Moon, Make It Rain, Blazing Torque, Tachyon Cutter, Shed Tail, and Hard Press moves; the Autograph, TM101, TM229, Dynamax Crystal ★And15, and Lastrange Ball items; and the four machine records Hard Press and TM101 reference. Records retain the fields read by the move and item services, with learners and holders limited to two. `flavor_text_entries` keep every English row in upstream order, plus the non-English rows after the last English one, so selection is exercised past trailing rows in other languages. They cover the flavor-text fallback (one and two English rows), a move with no flavor rows, the upstream `accuracy: 0` and `power: 0` placeholders, and the flavor-text placeholders: `N/A`, dash rows (`- - -`, `ー ー ー`), and unfilled game-text variables followed by a control code.

`handler-fixtures.ts` combines these captures with `domain-captures.json` and explicit synthetic records for the nine handler/resource suites. Synthetic dossiers copy non-identity fields solely to exercise wiring; those fields are not assertions about game data, except the past typing, abilities, and stats given to Pikachu and Clefairy, which PokéAPI served on 2026-11-25. Synthetic move, nature, and type payloads model fields consumed by each handler. Unknown test identifiers have explicit HTTP 404 routes. Every fixture uses `createFetchMock`, and `tests/setup.ts` fails unmatched fetch attempts even when handler error conversion catches the thrown error. The default lane never reaches the network; deliberate live checks run separately.
